methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
DroneForge is a pre-seed stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having raised $2.5M to date. The comparable universe consists of six private companies operating in Drones & Autonomous, including peers such as Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public comparables exist in this narrow segment.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to data constraints. The Stage-Progression approach uses the $2.5M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Pre-Seed to next-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $6M. A peer-median triangulation method could not be applied; while five same-sector peers exist, insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints preclude a statistically defensible narrow-peer median. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable dispersion risk.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5M to $7M, with a median point estimate of $6M. This range reflects the single stage-based method and incorporates typical conviction bands around pre-seed to seed progression. Key uncertainties include the absence of recent comparable financings at identical stage and the heterogeneity of drone/autonomous applications across the peer set—funding patterns and valuation multiples vary materially between last-mile delivery, urban air mobility, and industrial applications. Additional comparables or interim financing data would substantially narrow confidence intervals.
